newsitem.title: CANADA: ScotiaBank cuts loan loss provision.
newsitem.headline: ScotiaBank cuts loan loss provision.

text.p: The Bank of Nova Scotia said it cut its 1996 loan loss provision to an estimated C$380 million from last year's provision of C$560 million.

"Net impaired loans as a percentage of loans and acceptances are now at the lowest level since 1989," Canada's fourth largest bank said. New impaired loans fell to C$805 million, or 0.8 percent of loans and acceptances, from the previous quarter when they stood at 0.9 percent.
In the third quarter which ended July 31, the loan loss charged totalled C$95 million, flat from the last quarter but down C$33 million from a year earlier.
"The bank's general provision remains at C$325 milion, one of the highest of the Canadian banks," it said.
